AlternateTargets: a word that turns the case
Senses.Explanation: A turning word (轉語) is a single pivoting response that turns a stuck situation and settles a case. A master demands one — 'lay down a turning word' (下一轉語 / 著一轉語 / 道一轉語) — or supplies one in another's place (代一轉語). The locus classicus is Baizhang's wild fox: an old man, reborn five hundred times as a fox for once telling a student that a person of great conduct 'does not fall into cause-and-effect' (不落因果), begs Baizhang for a turning word said in his place (代一轉語); Baizhang's turning word — 'do not be blind to cause-and-effect' (不昧因果) — frees him. In the case commentaries masters challenge students to produce one: Wumen repeatedly challenges 'if right here you can lay down a turning word...' (若向者裏下得一轉語), and Xuedou invites 'let each Zen guest lay down a turning word' (請禪客各下一轉語). Baling gave his teacher Yunmen three turning words (三轉語) in place of a lineage-heir letter, and Yunmen said that on his memorial day he would simply cite those three and consider the debt repaid. The stakes of the fox case are stated in-corpus: 'answer a turning word wrongly and you fall into a fox's body' (錯答一轉語者，墮野狐身, the Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings 御選語錄, X68n1319); the case's paired answers survive in near parity — 'does not fall into cause-and-effect' (不落因果) 133 allowlist hits, 'not blind to cause-and-effect' (不昧因果) 126. Besides Baling's three, the record names 'Zhaozhou's three turning words shown to the assembly' (趙州示眾三轉語) (Blue Cliff case 96: 'Raised: Zhaozhou showed the assembly three turning words' 舉。趙州示眾三轉語, T48n2003; also X78n1556, J39nB441) — the three lines 'a golden buddha does not get through a furnace, a wooden buddha does not get through fire, a clay buddha does not get through water' (金佛不度爐。木佛不度火。泥佛不度水。) followed by 'the true buddha sits within' (真佛內裏坐) (X80n1565; 金佛不度爐 122 hits in 78 texts).
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide technical sense, shared across houses; no single master owns it. Multi-source across a lamp record (the Wudeng Huiyuan 五燈會元, 'Five Lamps Merged'), a case collection with comments (the Wumenguan 無門關, 'Gateless Checkpoint'), and case commentary (the Blue Cliff Record 碧巖錄), with distinct masters. Zen-allowlist grep counts: 'turning word' (轉語), 1,435 hits in 265 of 462 texts; 'a turning word' (一轉語) 877, 'lay down a turning word' (下一轉語) 185, 'three turning words' (三轉語) 157, 'a turning word in another's place' (代一轉語) 100, 'able to lay down a turning word' (下得一轉語) 88, 'say a turning word' (道一轉語) 16, 'set down a turning word' (著一轉語) 11, 'each lay down a turning word' (各下一轉語) 11, and the compact form 'lay down a turning word' (下轉語), 9.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今請和尚代一轉語。貴脫野狐身。師曰。汝問。老人曰。大修行人還落因果也無。師曰。不昧因果。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Section head names Chan Master Huaihai of Mount Baizhang in Hongzhou (洪州百丈山懷海禪師); the 'master' (師) is Baizhang. The fox-man asks for a turning word said in his place (代一轉語), and Baizhang's turning word is 'do not be blind to cause-and-effect' (不昧因果). The locus classicus of the term. (Wudeng Huiyuan 五燈會元.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 無門曰。且道。趙州頂草鞋意作麼生。若向者裏下得一轉語。便見南泉令不虛行。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 'Wumen says' (無門曰) — Wumen's stock challenge to the reader to produce a turning word, here on the Nanquan-cuts-the-cat / Zhaozhou-puts-sandals-on-his-head case. (Wumenguan, case 14.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 他日老僧忌辰只舉此三轉語。報恩足矣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 'Yunmen says' (雲門云) — Yunmen on the three turning words (三轉語) that his heir Baling Haojian offered him; he vows to cite only these on his memorial day and count the debt of kindness repaid. The three turning words themselves are Baling's. (Blue Cliff Record.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 雪竇復云。若要清風再復頭角重生。請禪客各下一轉語。問云。扇子既破。還我犀牛兒來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 'Xuedou again says' (雪竇復云) — Xuedou inviting each Zen guest to lay down a turning word on Yanguan's rhinoceros-fan case: 'the fan is already broken — bring me back the rhinoceros' (扇子既破。還我犀牛兒來). (Blue Cliff Record, case 91.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 今請闍黎別下一轉語。若愜老僧意。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Baiyan Mingzhe section. Baiyan Mingzhe is the exact speaker who asks the ācārya to lay down a different turning word and offers to open the gruel stores for the summer if it accords with his intent.
